summary: A clean, legible lesson: a flat squared band with a drafted, pressed-up rectangular tablet at the top, a chamfered rim and a sunk lozenge in its table. The idea reads at 300 px as 'a plaque / cartouche band', and the timeline is short and sensible. It is not yet a finished piece at Caiman's finish level. The 0.45 mm chamfer (fallback for the refused fillet) stacked on a 7 deg drafted wall gives the tablet a hard two-tier profile that reads as a bolt head or hex nut from the side, shoulder and reverse. The foot blend shows as a separate washer: in face.png a dark moat runs round the tablet between the wall and a raised skirt, and in hero.png a light ring sits outside the foot like a plate under it. The close-up (stones.png) shows combing and stair-step streaks on the right flank and the near-right corner of the tablet, and a wobbly foot blend. The lozenge, now cut as two mirrored triangles, reads as a sunk inverted pyramid rather than one bright-cut plane; it no longer looks like an arrow, but it is closer to an envelope flap or a stud than to a bright-cut. Every gate the JSON records is green, and the 'castable with care' verdict is the lesson Keystone is allowed to carry, but the report also records a 0.2 mm^2, -11 deg undercut on the chamfer flanks, which the lesson's exemption (zero-draft walls) does not cover.
strengths: One idea, face to palm: the tablet at the top, a plain squared band everywhere else; palm and sides carry nothing scattered.
Reads at 300 px without a caption as a cartouche or plaque band (read-test 2 passed and the final render holds that read).
Tablet now owns the top: about 85 to 90 percent of the band width, rounded corners, proud of the crest by 1.7 mm, the drafted skirt visible in hero and side.
The timeline is short and legible: band, plane, sketch, drafted boss, press-pull, chamfer, facet sketch, cut, mirror, each with its own frame.

Gates: watertight, 0 degenerate, 0 self-crossings on ring, parts and pattern, all 9 features Ok, 0 DFM findings, 0 obstructions and 0 unresolved rays at 0.100 and 0.075 mm, cold reload identical, 1.34 M triangles, template 1 patch within budget.

checklist.item: One idea face to palm, reads at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: hero-300 and face-300 read as a raised rectangular tablet on a plain band; nothing else competes. The facet inside it reads as a sunk diamond, which supports rather than splits the idea.

checklist.item: Finished piece a jeweller would sell: proportion, weight, every part meeting the band
checklist.reason: The tablet meets the band through a visible washer: a dark moat between wall and skirt in face.png (all four sides) and a light ring outside the foot in hero.png and bare-vs-finished.png. From the side, shoulder and reverse, the drafted wall plus 0.45 mm chamfer reads as a hex-nut head bolted on. The band is right in weight (6.0 x 2.0) but the tablet is short round the ring for the width it covers, so it looks like a badge rather than a cartouche grown from the band.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD: edges broken, seams blended, no slabs
checklist.reason: Chamfer-on-draft gives two hard flat bands at the rim (shoulder.png, reverse.png). Band edges carry only a 0.15 mm edge round, so the band reads as a cut sheet on palm.png. The foot blend (0.6 mm) is there but renders as a step, not a run-in.

checklist.item: Outlines render crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: stones.png (close-up): vertical streaks and stair-steps on the right flank and near-right corner of the tablet, a wobbling foot blend line along the near long side, and smeared shading inside the lozenge cut. face.png shows small notches at the inner corners of the rim chamfer. hero-300 is clean at that size.

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: No stones by design; stones_previewed 0 = stones_reported 0.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not a factory stock (Flat 6.0 x 2.0 with flatten_sides); the squared band keeps its square walls.

checklist.item: Lesson legible in timeline.png, one visible step per feature, short sensible order
checklist.reason: Nine frames, each adds a visible step. Weak spots: frame 5 (press-pull) is barely distinguishable from frame 4 at timeline size, and frame 8 shows only faint lines; the cut only reads in frame 9. Nine features against the planned eight (Mirror added) is acceptable.

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from the other Officina rings and the starter gallery
checklist.reason: A squared band with a single raised tablet is distinct from Rivet's domed strap, Sigil's stock seal and the stone starters; closest neighbour is the Court band, which it differs from by the tablet.

punch_list.zone: Tablet foot, all round (feature 4 'Drafted boss' Join blend, feature 2 plane offset), theta 84 to 96 deg
punch_list.change: Remove the washer and moat at the foot. The tablet should rise out of the band through one continuous concave run-in. Reduce the sink of the work plane (offset -0.7 toward -0.45 mm, just past the 0.41 mm sag) so the boss foot sits at band level instead of in a pocket, and keep blend_mm 0.6 but make sure the blend is the only transition (no flat step between blend and wall).
punch_list.acceptance: face.png shows no dark rectangular moat between the tablet wall and the band on any side; hero.png shows one soft highlight running from the wall down into the band, with no separate light ring outside the foot.

punch_list.zone: Tablet top rim (feature 6 'Chamfer the rim') and drafted wall
punch_list.change: Get rid of the hex-nut profile and the chamfer-flank undercut. Retry a native Fillet at a radius that fits (0.25 to 0.3 mm instead of 0.35) on the rim edges; if it is still refused, cut the chamfer to 0.25 mm and give it a 0.1 mm soft edge, or raise the wall draft from 7 to 10 deg so the chamfer no longer leans back across the parting plane.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png, shoulder.png and reverse.png the tablet rim shows one rounded or single narrow bright line, not two flat steps; report.json field_notes no longer list an undercut on #6 (0 mm^2 undercut, worst draft >= 0 deg).

punch_list.zone: Tablet flanks and corners, theta 87 to 93 deg (right flank and near-right corner in stones.png); lozenge cut (features 8, 9)
punch_list.change: Clear the combing and stair-steps: raise tessellation density on the drafted wall and corner arcs and on the blend, and make the lozenge cut floors planar with no smoothing across their ridge.
punch_list.acceptance: stones.png at full size shows no vertical streaks or stair-steps on any tablet flank, a smooth foot line on the near side, flat tone in each lozenge facet, and no notches at the inner corners of the rim in face.png.

punch_list.change: Break the band's outer edges from 0.15 to about 0.35 mm, keeping the squared section, so the band stops reading as cut sheet.
punch_list.acceptance: palm.png and hero.png show a thin continuous highlight along both outer edges of the band; the band still reads square in side.png.

punch_list.zone: report.json authored block; README lesson text
punch_list.change: State the 'castable with care' verdict as the lesson in the authored block (zero-draft walls and table, as with a signet), and record the measured low-draft share, so the exemption is explained in the report itself, not only by field notes.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json authored contains a verdict explanation naming the zero-draft walls and the measured 29 percent low-draft share, with no remaining undercut note.

punch_list.change: Make the press-pull and the first facet cut visible as steps: press-pull distance 0.8 should show as a visibly taller wall versus frame 4 (or render the timeline at a slightly closer camera), and frame 8 should show the cut triangle in tone, not as faint lines.
